summary: WebRender received substantial performance and rendering improvements across multiple areas: gradient, border, and glyph rendering now compute geometry once in the display list builder (avoiding redundant work), support for CSS `corner-shape` enables true superellipse borders, **glyphs now use four-pixel positioning accuracy in rotated text**, and embedded bitmap glyphs are applied at their final size instead of scaled after rendering. The team also improved Metal integration for ANGLE-based WebGL, refactored internal resource management to share GPU buffers between draw calls, and fixed various edge cases in clipping, anti-aliasing, and blur clamping across different device pixel scales.
